# jsonstor-browser

> Home: [http://jsonstor.liquicode.com](http://jsonstor.liquicode.com)
>
> Version: 0.1.0

### The browser storages: local storage, the Origin Private File System, and IndexedDB.

Overview
---------------------------------------------------------------------

`jsonstor` defines one interface for working with a document store and implements it
  for a variety of database products and file formats. The interface is the same whichever
  adapter is underneath, so the storage a project uses becomes a configuration decision
  rather than a structural one.

This package is one such adapter. The browser storages: local storage, the Origin Private File System, and IndexedDB.

***It carries no database driver.*** The server is reached over HTTP with the runtime's
  own `fetch`, so this package adds nothing to a project beyond `jsonstor` and `jsongin`.

See [`@liquicode/jsonstor`](https://github.com/liquicode/jsonstor) for the interface,
  and [jsonstor.liquicode.com](http://jsonstor.liquicode.com) for the documentation.

Getting Started
---------------------------------------------------------------------

```bash
npm install --save @liquicode/jsonstor-browser
```

```js
const jsonstor = require( '@liquicode/jsonstor' )();
jsonstor.LoadPlugin( require( '@liquicode/jsonstor-browser' ) );

let storage = jsonstor.GetStorage( 'jsonstor-browser', {
	Key: '...',
	Path: '...',
	DatabaseName: '...',
	CollectionName: '...',
	AutoFlush: true,
	PrimaryKey: "_id",
	PrimaryKeyMutable: false,
	HostIndex: false,
} );
```

Versions
---------------------------------------------------------------------

This package answers to more than one name. Pass any of these to `GetStorage()`;
  a name which is not listed is refused.

| Name | Dialect it uses | Measured against |
|------|-----------------|------------------|
| `jsonstor-browser-localstorage` | its own | - |
| `jsonstor-browser-opfs` | its own | - |
| `jsonstor-browser-indexeddb` | its own | - |

A name with its own dialect was measured against that server version and covers every
  later one up to the next such name. The rest resolve to one of those. The bare name
  follows the newest dialect this package carries, which is what most callers want.

A name whose dialect your server cannot serve is refused on the first operation, naming
  the version you asked for and the one the server needs.

Settings
---------------------------------------------------------------------

| Setting | Required | Default | Description |
|---|:---:|:---:|---|
| `Key` | ***Yes*** | - | ***`jsonstor-browser-localstorage` only.*** The `localStorage` key this collection is stored under. One key holds one collection; name a second key for a second collection. |
| `Path` | ***Yes*** | - | ***`jsonstor-browser-opfs` only.*** The path within the Origin Private File System holding this collection. Folders along it are created as needed. |
| `DatabaseName` | ***Yes*** | - | ***`jsonstor-browser-indexeddb` only.*** The IndexedDB database holding this collection. It is created if it does not exist. |
| `CollectionName` | ***Yes*** | - | ***`jsonstor-browser-indexeddb` only.*** The object store this storage reads and writes. One database holds as many collections as you name. |
| `AutoFlush` | No | `true` | ***The two blob storages only.*** Write the collection out after every insert, update, replacement or delete. Turn it off to batch a run of writes and call `FlushStorage()` yourself. `jsonstor-browser-indexeddb` writes a record at a time and has nothing to flush. |
| `PrimaryKey` | No | `"_id"` | The document field which is the identifier. Name the field an existing store is already keyed on to read one. |
| `PrimaryKeyMutable` | No | `false` | Allow an update or a replacement to change the identifier. Off by default, so an operation which would move it is refused by name rather than silently discarded. |
| `HostIndex` | No | `false` | ***The two blob storages only.*** Hold an index over the identifier, so a lookup by it costs one entry rather than the whole collection. Off by default, because an index over a store something else writes goes stale - call `RefreshIndex()` when it might have. `jsonstor-browser-indexeddb` hosts its own index and takes no such setting. |

Peculiarities
---------------------------------------------------------------------

- ***This package runs in a browser and nowhere else.*** None of these three APIs exists in Node, and constructing one there is refused by name rather than left to fail on the first read. Load it from the browser bundle, beside `jsonstor` itself.
- ***The package name is not a storage.*** `jsonstor-browser` names three mechanisms which are not interchangeable, so asking for it refuses and names the three. Ask for `jsonstor-browser-localstorage`, `jsonstor-browser-opfs` or `jsonstor-browser-indexeddb`.
- ***All three are primes and none is a version.*** A caller choosing between them is choosing a quota, a write path and a failure mode. There is no floor to compare and no boundary to cross, so `StorageInfo()` reports the dialect asked for and the `jsongin` which decides its queries - a version number for a browser API would be a fiction.
- ***`jsonstor-browser-localstorage` keeps the whole collection under one key, as one JSON string.*** `localStorage` has no partial update and no useful ordering, so a document per key would cost a read of every key on every query and buy nothing. This is `jsonstor-jsonfile` with `setItem` where `writeFileSync` is.
- ***An origin gets about 5MB of `localStorage`, and that is the whole of what that dialect can hold.*** Measured at 4.96MB in Chrome 152, shared with everything else that origin stores. A write past it raises `QuotaExceededError`, which the adapter lets through rather than swallowing - so the failing write is named, instead of leaving you a storage which quietly stopped persisting. ***Use `jsonstor-browser-opfs` for a collection with any size to it***; it has about ten gigabytes.
- ***`jsonstor-browser-opfs` is the browser storage with room.*** An origin gets about ten gigabytes of OPFS where `localStorage` gets about five megabytes, measured on one origin in Chrome 152. ***That is the reason to choose it***, and it is the only one: a collection which fits in `localStorage` is better served by `jsonstor-browser-localstorage`, which needs no `await` to read itself.
- ***`jsonstor-browser-indexeddb` is the only one of the three which is not a blob.*** The other two serialize the whole collection on every write; this one stores a record per document, so a large collection costs one write per document changed rather than one write of everything.
- ***And it is the only adapter in the family with no server which hosts its own index.*** `StorageInfo()` reports `IndexHostedBy: "database"`: the unique index over the identifier is IndexedDB's, it enforces uniqueness, and it answers a lookup by identifier without reading the collection. ***So `RefreshIndex()` answers 0 and means it*** - there is nothing there that could be out of step with the documents.
- ***In IndexedDB a record is not the document.*** Each record carries an auto-incrementing sequence, the encoded identifier, and the document itself. ***The store is keyed on the sequence rather than on the identifier***, because IndexedDB iterates in key order: keying on the identifier would make a collection read back sorted by it, where every adapter in this family reads back in the order it was written.
- ***The identifier is indexed in its encoded form, and that is not decoration.*** IndexedDB refuses a boolean, a null and an object as a key outright - and an *index* over such a value does not fail, it ***silently skips the record***, so a raw index would have stopped enforcing uniqueness for exactly the identifiers it could not represent. The encoded form is a string for every value, which is the answer `jsonstor-couchdb` reached when CouchDB refused a numeric identifier.
- ***A document is stored as JSON would have stored it.*** IndexedDB's structured clone is more faithful than JSON - a `Date` comes back a `Date`, and a member set to `undefined` survives - and both are deliberately kept out. Every other storage in this family round-trips through JSON, and an adapter which returned a `Date` where every sibling returns a string would be a portability trap rather than a feature.
- ***None of the three has a query language, so every criteria is decided by `jsongin`.*** Nothing is pre-filtered beyond IndexedDB's lookup by identifier: a read walks the collection and each document is tested in this process. That is always the right answer and it costs the whole collection.
- ***Every tab of an origin shares one store.*** The two blob dialects cache the collection in memory, so another tab writing the same key or path leaves both the documents and the index stale. `RefreshIndex()` re-reads and rebuilds from what is really there.
- ***A collection reads back in the order it was written.*** Use `FindMany2` with a `Sort` when you need a different order.

Storage Interface
---------------------------------------------------------------------

Every adapter implements the same functions, and they are documented once:
  [Storage Interface](http://jsonstor.liquicode.com/#/guides/Storage-Interface.md).

***The operator list is not repeated here.*** A criteria, a projection, and an update are
  the engine's, and the list changes whenever the engine gains an operator - a copy in this
  file could only ever be out of date. See the
  [Operator Reference](https://github.com/liquicode/jsongin/blob/main/docs/guides/Operator-Reference.md).
